feedback: Although deterministic validation is valid, repair the semantic logic: do not make this optional in-lieu approval pathway mandatory for every ship targeted by sh:targetClass nltl:ship; constrain it to an individual ship using the alternative Ke/RCH method, without inventing a convenience applicability boolean. Ensure approvalRevocationStatus cannot be Draft, Submitted, UnderReview, Rejected, or Expired while approvalStatus is true; the current independent requirements allow an approved=true ship with a rejected or otherwise non-approved state to pass. Restrict the status semantics to the verified approval/revocation states and encode their consistency, while retaining the required alternative-calculation/model-test evidence and at least one Ke or RCH result. Do not add shipPerformanceExperienceEvidence, because the COMPLETE dependency contract explicitly removes that nonmandatory evidence obligation.

Repair the applicability and target logic. Do not target every ship that happens to have any one evidence or result, then make the alternative-method evidence, approval/status, and Ke-or-RCH result obligations mandatory for that target set. Constrain the shape to an individual ship actually using the optional in-lieu method, with the required alternative-calculation or model-test evidence and at least one Ke or RCH result; do not invent an applicability boolean. Preserve both result alternatives and their declared units, and retain the approvalStatus/approvalRevocationStatus consistency rule so approvalStatus true requires evidenceStateApproved. The deterministic graph is structurally valid, but its broad OR-based SPARQL target creates accidental applicability and imposes the pathway on ships not established as using it.
